newsitem.title: USA: Golden Books aims for breakeven EBITDA.
newsitem.headline: Golden Books aims for breakeven EBITDA.

text.p: Golden Books Family Entertainment Inc said Tuesday that its 1997 goal is to make enough progress in the second half of the year to reach break-even earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) before transition costs.
In 1996, Golden Books reported negative EBITDA of $38 million.
The company said in a statement that it intends to make enough progress to report single digit sales growth in its publishing business.
Benefits from its sales force reorganization, the establishment of Golden Value Books, Futech sound technology and its licensing portfolio should begin to show results in 1998, Golden Books said.

In a separate statement, Golden Books and Parachute Publishing said they have reached an agreement to publish 65 new books by R.L. Stine, the author of children's thrillers such as the "Goosebumps" series.
Golden Books has rights to publish titles of Stine's "Fear Street," a series of thrillers for 8-to 14-year-olds.
